name: Mary Barra

career.title: Co-op student and quality inspector, inspecting fender panels and hoods
Engineering and staff roles, incl. head of internal communications
Head of Global Product Development (adding Global Purchasing and Supply Chain in 2013)

background_rationale: An electrical engineer who started at GM as an 18-year-old co-op student and rose through manufacturing engineering, plant management and product development before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: After an internal investigation by attorney Anton Valukas into GM's delayed ignition-switch recall, Barra dismissed 15 employees, disciplined five others and set up a victim compensation program run by Kenneth Feinberg.
GM announced a goal to end production and sales of fossil-fuel light vehicles by 2035 and become carbon neutral by 2040; those EV plans were largely scaled back in 2025.
GM stopped funding Cruise's robotaxi business and folded its autonomous-driving work into driver-assistance systems for personal vehicles, taking full ownership of Cruise in early 2025.

personal_story.hook: Mary Barra's first GM job, at 18, was inspecting fenders and hood panels on an assembly line.
personal_story.summary: Barra grew up near Detroit, the daughter of a die maker who worked 39 years at GM's Pontiac division and a mother raised in poverty on a Michigan farm during the Great Depression; she says both believed hard work and education could take you anywhere. A cousin's Chevrolet Camaro helped spark her interest in engineering. At 18 she entered GM's co-op program through General Motors Institute, starting as a quality inspector checking fenders and hood panels at the Pontiac plant. GM later sponsored her MBA at Stanford, and she worked through communications, plant management, manufacturing engineering, human resources and product development roles. In January 2014 she became the first woman to lead a global automaker.
